question: An AND gate is used in a digital circuit to enable a certain function. Under what condition will the function be enabled?

options.text: When any one of the inputs is low
When all the inputs are high
When any one of the inputs is high
When all the inputs are low

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

An AND gate is a fundamental logic gate used in digital circuits. It performs a logical conjunction operation, meaning it outputs a HIGH signal (1) only when all its inputs are HIGH (1). Otherwise, the output remains LOW (0). This behavior makes it a key component in enabling specific functions in digital systems when certain conditions are met.

The AND gate has two or more inputs and one output. Its operation can be described using a truth table:

 
 

 Input A
 Input B
 Output (A × B)

From the truth table, it is evident that the AND gate produces a HIGH output only when all inputs are HIGH.

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 2:** When all the inputs are high.

This option accurately describes the behavior of an AND gate. The function enabled by the AND gate will work only when all the input signals are HIGH (1). This is the fundamental property of an AND gate, as demonstrated in the truth table above. For example, in a digital circuit controlling access to a system, all required conditions must be satisfied (i.e., all inputs HIGH) for the system to be activated
